verdict.rationale: WezTerm documents a `wezterm cli` subcommand that drives a running GUI or multiplexer instance to spawn programs and manipulate tabs and panes. A hands-on runtime probe confirmed the whole control loop with no GUI session: `spawn --new-window` returned a pane-id, `send-text` delivered input, `get-text` read the pane back and `list` enumerated windows, tabs and panes. A community user separately cites get-text for dumping scrollback. Missing for 10: the pack has only the CLI index summary, not detailed first-party reference pages for each subcommand (send-text, get-text, list).

support.subject: As a developer, I can script and control the terminal from the command line — open windows, send text, query state — via a documented CLI or IPC interface

citations.quote: The _cli_ subcommand interacts with a running wezterm GUI or multiplexer instance, and can be used to spawn programs and manipulate tabs and panes.

`wezterm cli spawn --new-window` returned a pane-id, `wezterm cli send-text --pane-id N "echo PA_PROBE_OK"` delivered, `wezterm cli get-text` read the pane content back, `wezterm cli list` enumerated windows/tabs/panes; no GUI session required.
